evidence.title: Truman Capote
evidence.text: Truman Garcia Capote ( ; born Truman Streckfus Persons, September 30, 1924 – August 25, 1984) was an American novelist, screenwriter, playwright, and actor.

evidence.title: Truman Capote
evidence.text: Many of Capote's short stories, novels, plays, and nonfiction are recognized as literary classics, including the novella "Breakfast at Tiffany's" (1958) and the true crime novel "In Cold Blood" (1966), which he labeled a "nonfiction novel".

evidence.title: Truman Capote
evidence.text: At least 20 films and television dramas have been produced of Capote novels, stories, and plays.

evidence.title: Capote (film)

evidence.title: Capote (film)
evidence.text: Philip Seymour Hoffman won several awards, including the Academy Award for Best Actor, for his critically acclaimed portrayal of the title character.

evidence.title: Capote (film)
evidence.text: The film was based on Gerald Clarke's biography "Capote" and was directed by Bennett Miller.

evidence.title: Capote (film)
evidence.text: It was filmed mostly in Manitoba in the autumn of 2004.

evidence.title: Capote (film)
evidence.text: It was released September 30, 2005, to coincide with Truman Capote's birthday.

evidence.title: Truman Capote Literary Trust
evidence.text: The Truman Capote Literary Trust is an American charitable trust established in 1994 by Truman Capote's literary executor, Alan U. Schwartz, pursuant to Capote's will.

evidence.title: A Christmas Memory
evidence.text: "A Christmas Memory" is a short story by Truman Capote.

evidence.title: A Christmas Memory
evidence.text: Originally published in "Mademoiselle" magazine in December 1956, it was reprinted in "The Selected Writings of Truman Capote" in 1963.

evidence.title: A Christmas Memory
evidence.text: It was issued in a stand-alone hardcover edition by Random House in 1966, and it has been published in many editions and anthologies since.

evidence.title: Infamous (film)
evidence.text: Infamous is a 2006 American drama film based on the 1997 book by George Plimpton "Truman Capote: In Which Various Friends, Enemies, Acquaintances, and Detractors Recall His Turbulent Career".

evidence.title: Infamous (film)
evidence.text: It covers the period from the late 1950s through the mid-1960s, during which Truman Capote researched and wrote his bestseller "In Cold Blood".
